claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my daughter Alex. She's 11 years old and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you at home.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't know if anyone else is claiming for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask another important question:

**Does Alex live with anyone else, or does she live solely with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning do you provide for her needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, of course - I'm her parent and I look after her. I provide everything she needs - food, clothes, a home, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of that. She's just at home with me, living a normal life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes. I'm settled here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility criteria:

✓ Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
✓ You are responsible for her - you provide her food, clothes, and accommodation
✓ She lives with you at home
✓ You live in the UK and are settled here
✓ Alex is not in hospital or care
✓ No one else appears to be claiming Child Benefit for her

**Next steps:**
You can go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit. You'll need to apply to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC).

**Please note:** If you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. Even if this applies to you, you can still claim Child Benefit - you would just need to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
